subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Third Wave: Coffee as Craft
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Third Wave: Coffee as Craft usable.

hook.text: The 'third wave' treats coffee like wine—obsessing over origin, variety, processing, and the individual farmer who grew it.

buildup.text: First wave was commodity (Folgers). Second wave was café culture (Starbucks). Third wave elevates coffee to craft.

discovery.text: Third-wave roasters buy single-origin, traceable lots. They roast light to showcase terroir and score coffees like wine critics.

twist.text: Critics argue third wave is elitist—$7 pour-overs alienate everyday drinkers and ignore the global majority who drink instant.

climax.text: A possible 'fourth wave' focuses on equity—paying farmers fairly while making quality accessible, not just exclusive.

punchline.text: Commodity, culture, craft, equity. Each wave remakes what coffee means.

quiz.question: What defines third-wave coffee?
options: Treating coffee as artisanal craft — focusing on origin, variety, and terroir
